impact_summary: GET /api/v1/items/ gains an optional case-insensitive `search` parameter that filters by title (icontains, autoescaped) and is combined with the existing owner filter. The previous separate superuser/non-superuser branches were refactored into a single shared filter list, with the count and the page both using the same filters. The Items page gets a search input (data-testid=item-search) that re-queries the API and shows 'No items match your search' when nothing matches. The refactor touches the owner-scoping logic, so there is some risk of a regression in access control.

cases_to_review.reason: Owner scoping in read_items was refactored into a shared filter list. Confirm a user still sees only their own items, with and without `search`.
The list endpoint signature changed. Confirm it still requires authentication.
The Items page render path and query key changed (['items', search]). Confirm the list still shows only the logged-in user's items.
The query key changed, so the list refresh after a UI create may behave differently. Verify the new item still appears.
Edit relies on the items list refreshing under the new query key. Verify the edited title is shown.
Delete relies on the items list refreshing under the new query key. Verify the item disappears.

new_cases.title: Search items by title is case-insensitive and scoped to the caller's own items
steps: Create two fresh normal users, A and B, and obtain a token for each
As A, create items titled 'Alpha-<uuid>-Report' and 'Beta-<uuid>-Notes'
As B, create an item titled 'alpha-<uuid>-Other' (same uuid token in the title, different case)
As A, call GET /api/v1/items/?search=ALPHA-<uuid> with A's token
new_cases.expected: Status is 200. data contains exactly one item, A's 'Alpha-<uuid>-Report'. B's item is not returned despite matching the search, and A's 'Beta' item is excluded. count is 1, so the search is case-insensitive and still scoped to the owner.

new_cases.title: Items page search box filters the list and shows the no-match message
steps: Create a fresh user through the API and log in through the UI
Create two items via the API with unique titles, 'Apple-<uuid>' and 'Banana-<uuid>'
Type 'apple-<uuid>' into the input with data-testid='item-search'
Verify only the Apple row is visible and the Banana row is not
new_cases.expected: After the first search the table shows only 'Apple-<uuid>' and not 'Banana-<uuid>'. After the no-match search the page shows 'No items match your search' and 'Try a different search term'.
